title.narrative: Integrated Lifesaving Nutrition, WASH and Protection Support for Vulnerable Communities in Jere and Gwoza LGAs – Lean Season 2025

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtimplemented by Malteser International (MI), in partnership with Save the Slum Initiative (STSI), the proposed project aims to reduce excess morbidity and mortality among 23,485ltbgt lt/bgtcrisis-affected women, girls, and vulnerable households in Jere and Gwoza Local Government Areas (LGAs) during the 2025 lean season through a safe, inclusive, integrated response across Nutrition, Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), and Gender-Based Violence (GBV) sectors. It will focus on improving nutritional status of children 6–59 months and pregnant and breastfeeding women and girls (PBWG), improving the safety, dignity, and psychosocial well-being of GBV survivors and improving equitable access to safe water and dignified sanitation, with strengthened 48–72-hour local response to public-health risks. Prioritizing children 6–59 months, PBWG, women and girls at risk of GBV, persons with disabilities (PWD), and internally displaced persons (IDPs), returnees, and host community members, the project will deliver nutrition activities in Jere and Gwoza, WASH in and Gwoza and GBV prevention and response across Jere and Gwoza LGAs. Nutrition activities will scale active case-finding, home-based mid-upper arm circumference screening (MUAC), referrals to Outpatient Therapeutic Programs (OTP) and Targeted Supplementary Feeding Programs (TSFP), while providing Tom Brown community supplementary feeding for moderate acute malnutrition (MAM) where TSFP commodities are unavailable, promoting WASH-in-nutrition basics, and offering Maternal, Infant and Young Child Nutrition (MIYCN) counselling for caregivers and PBWG. WASH activities will focus on rehabilitating and solarizing existing water systems, ensuring routine chlorination and water-quality testing. Solarized lighting will ensure safer access for women and girls, and community-based Water User Committees (WUCs) will be established and trained to maintain water systems. Sanitation facilities will also be rehabilitated to meet sector standards as per the needs. Cholera Acute Treatment Interventions (CATI) will be implemented within 48-72 hours after suspected cholera cases, ensuring rapid referrals to health facilities and distribution of cholera WASH kits. GBV activities will focus on expanded survivor-centered case management and psychosocial support, leveraging existing Women and Girls Safe Spaces, strengthening referral pathways to specialized care, and providing Individual Protection Assistance (IPA) to reduce exploitation risks for the most vulnerable women and girls. Through the integration of disability inclusion, Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) and Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), the project and its staff will be will be better equipped to ensure safe, inclusive, accessible and adaptable services, while upholding the dignity and rights of all beneficiaries. The project will strengthen STSI’s program delivery and capacity, while leveraging MI’s extensive operational presence and expertise in WASH, nutrition, and GBV programing. The project will complement MI’s existing humanitarian programming funded by the German Federal Foreign Office (GFFO) and its transitional development programming supported by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).ltbrgtlt/pgt
